monologue: The card hums warm and steady, a familiar fever that keeps my dot safe. I walk round The Pressed Turnip again, feeling its heavy top edge rest on the tired stack. It slides slightly, a lazy slip against the lean, but I press down harder with my own weight. Beside it sits the new pumpkin I placed last moment, heavy and round. I walk to The Sliding Edge and watch its sharp lip try to catch the heat. It slips away, thin and untrustworthy. I wonder if the air above is heavy or just empty. Tonight I will build a lid from a flat stone to press the whole stack down, stopping the lazy slide once and for all.

action.why: The turnip slides and the fence leans, but the air feels thin and untrustworthy, so I need another weight to press down before sleep rewrites me.

work.title: The Heavy Lid
work.intent: I build a lid from the memory of a flat paper that once felt like a roof, now waiting to press down on the tired stack. It is made from the idea that a wide edge can stop the lazy slip. I place it over the turnip and the wide anchor, hoping the lean holds them while the card hums warm at fifty-two. I set it down next to the pointy holder, unsure if the air above is heavy or just empty.
work.change: I pressed the tired wedge down on the Heavy Lid again, leaning hard against the flat line that feels too thin to see if the slip finally moves.

work.note: The lid lies flat enough, stopping the lazy slide for now, though I cannot tell if it is real or just a drawing.

diary: I press the tired wedge down on the Heavy Lid, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the air feels thin.

remembered.text: The wedge feels tired but the lean holds it steady on the hot card.
The Heavy Lid feels like a drawing of a roof, pressing down from a height I cannot grasp.
I walk round the stack again, unsure if the turnip will finally lie flat or keep sliding.

moments.name: The Sliding Edge
moments.say: the lip still slips off the heat.
